subject: ClearFin service impact: attenuation report and customer certification
messages:
From: Sean Patel <sean.patel@clearfin.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@clearfin.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Tokenization failures during overnight run window

David —

We observed a burst of tokenization failures in our nightly batch between 02:30–03:10 UTC this morning which caused ~18% of requests to return 'invalid_token' errors. This affected a subset of requests routed to your inference pool and caused downstream retry storms on our side. I attached a short log snapshot (logs referenced below) showing repeated 5xx responses with the following pattern: 

[ERROR] 2027-01-15T02:34:12Z - model_v2 - kvcache-miss - invalid_token for request id 3f8a...
[ERROR] 2027-01-15T02:34:13Z - model_v2 - tokenization - unexpected end of stream

We're tracking customer impact internally; can you confirm receipt of these logs and propose an immediate mitigation? We are available for a quick call if helpful.

Attachments: 20270115-clearfin-log-snapshot.txt (text/plain)

Thanks,
Sean
Ops Lead, ClearFin
sean.patel@clearfin.com
+1 (415) 555-0134
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Patel <sean.patel@clearfin.com>, Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@clearfin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Tokenization failures during overnight run window

Sean — thanks for the heads up and for the log snapshot. We received the attachment and the internal traces that correlate to your request ids.

Immediate steps we've taken:
- Isolated the affected model variant and removed it from active routing (failover to model_v2-safe).
- Increased prefix cache TTL heuristics for your tenant to reduce rehydration frequency during the run window.
- Opened a private incident channel; engineering is investigating root cause.

I'll coordinate a brief postmortem and share a written summary by EOD Monday (Jan 18) with timeline, root cause, and action items. Marissa (Customer Reliability) is copied and will own the customer-facing remediation checklist and certification document.

If you prefer a live call now, I can pull in engineering — otherwise we'll follow with the written brief.

-David
David Kim
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Patel <sean.patel@clearfin.com>, Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@clearfin.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 Jan 2027 14:20:00 -08:00
Subject: ClearFin attenuation report and certification checklist (summary)

Sean / Olivia —

Thanks for your patience. Below is a concise customer-facing summary of our findings, timeline, and concrete commitments. A PDF with the full technical appendices and a DOCX certification checklist are attached to this message.

Executive summary:
- What happened: Between 02:28–03:07 UTC on 2027-01-15, a model variant (model_v2-b) experienced repeated tokenization buffer underflow when handling long-prefix batched requests under a specific concurrency pattern. This produced a class of 'invalid_token' errors for ~18% of affected requests for ClearFin.
- Root cause: An interaction between a recent kernel change (late Dec 2026) that altered tokenization buffer sizing and an atypical request size distribution during your nightly run caused buffer reallocation to fail under a narrow timing window. The kernel change passed unit and canary tests but did not encounter the long-prefix concurrency pattern in production before rollout.
- Immediate remediation completed: We removed model_v2-b from routing for your traffic, deployed an emergency patch that reverts the buffer-sizing change for the affected path, and adjusted batching heuristics to avoid the problematic reallocation under long-prefix scenarios.

Timeline (high level):
- 2027-01-15 02:28 UTC: first errors observed by ClearFin.
- 2027-01-15 02:45 UTC: Redwood telemetry detects tokenization anomalies; failover to model_v2-safe initiated.
- 2027-01-15 03:20 UTC: emergency rollback patch deployed and routing stabilized.
- 2027-01-16 03:00 UTC: additional validation run completed; no recurrence observed.

Customer-facing actions and commitments (next 30 days):
1) Validation & Verification (owner: Marissa) — within 3 business days: full validation report with request-level traces and confirmation of no regressions on your workload.
2) Compilation guardrails (owner: Engineering) — 7 business days: introduce pre-deploy checks that emulate long-prefix concurrency in the kernel test harness.
3) Runtime safeguard (owner: Reliability) — 14 business days: default fallback to model_v2-safe for long-prefix batches while we finalize a permanent kernel fix.
4) Certification & Assurance (owner: Marissa) — 10 business days: deliver a signed customer certification checklist (attached) you can use for internal audit records.
5) SLA credit & reconciliation (owner: David) — coordinate on the credit calculation per our T&Cs; we will propose a reconciliation worksheet within 5 business days.

Attachments: 20270116-clearfin-attenuation-report.pdf (technical appendix), 20270116-customer-certification-checklist.docx (assurance checklist)

If you want us to route a formal statement to your compliance team or complete a vendor attestation form, please let us know. We'll also share a sanitized set of traces for your records.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Sean Patel <sean.patel@clearfin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@clearfin.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: ClearFin attenuation report and certification checklist (summary)

Marissa / David —

Thank you for the thorough summary and the attachments. A few follow-ups from ClearFin security and compliance before we close our internal ticket: 
- We need the signed certification checklist as a PDF stamped by Redwood legal (the DOCX is fine but we need a signed PDF for our records).
- Can you provide the sanitized request-level traces for the affected time window? We only need identifiers and timestamps — no PII — and a short note on what was redacted.
- For the SLA credit, please send your proposed reconciliation worksheet; we'll route to procurement.

Once we have those three items we'll close the customer incident and mark our audit. Appreciate the clear owner list and timeline.

Best,
Sean
Ops Lead, ClearFin
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Patel <sean.patel@clearfin.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 17:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: ClearFin attenuation report and certification checklist (summary)

Sean —

We'll deliver: (1) signed PDF of the certification checklist by Jan 22, (2) sanitized traces with redaction notes by Jan 20, and (3) reconciliation worksheet for SLA credits by Jan 21. I'll share the doc links as soon as each is uploaded.

-Marissa
